title: A Tap at the Back, a Drain at the Front

scenes.tts: What helps set the front edges of the Hox code? A signal made from vitamin A.
scenes.visual: Title card: A Tap at the Back, a Drain at the Front. The rhombomere row with question marks at each domain edge.
scenes.narration: What helps set the front edges of the Hox code? A signal made from vitamin A.

scenes.tts: Retinoic acid is made from retinol, which is vitamin A, in two steps. Raldh two, the main enzyme for the last step, is made in mesoderm beside the posterior hindbrain and spinal cord.
scenes.caption: Retinoic acid is made from retinol, which is vitamin A, in two steps. Raldh2, the main enzyme for the last step, is made in mesoderm beside the posterior hindbrain and spinal cord.
scenes.visual: Retinol converts to retinaldehyde, then to retinoic acid; two arrows labelled oxidation, the second labelled Raldh2. Then mesoderm beside the back of the hindbrain and the spinal cord glows: the tap.
scenes.narration: Retinoic acid is made from retinol, which is vitamin A, in two steps. Raldh2, the main enzyme for the last step, is made in mesoderm beside the posterior hindbrain and spinal cord.

scenes.tts: Cyp twenty-six enzymes destroy it. Cyp twenty-six A one is strong toward the front of the neural plate.
scenes.caption: Cyp26 enzymes destroy it. Cyp26a1 is strong toward the front of the neural plate.
scenes.visual: The front of the neural plate glows, labelled Cyp26a1: the drain.
scenes.narration: Cyp26 enzymes destroy it. Cyp26a1 is strong toward the front of the neural plate.

scenes.tts: Picture a bath, with the tap at the back and the drain at the front. Retinoic acid ends up high at the back and low at the front.
scenes.visual: A long bath drawn under the rhombomere row: tap at the back, drain at the front. Dye from the tap is darkest near it; a concentration curve rises from front to back, labelled: schematic, not a measured profile. Small caption: like dye in the water, not the water level, which evens out.
scenes.narration: Picture a bath, with the tap at the back and the drain at the front. Retinoic acid ends up high at the back and low at the front.

scenes.tts: In the nucleus, it binds the retinoic acid receptor, R A R. R A R pairs with its partner, R X R, on short DNA sequences called response elements.
scenes.caption: In the nucleus, it binds the retinoic acid receptor, RAR. RAR pairs with its partner, RXR, on short DNA sequences called response elements.
scenes.visual: A retinoic acid molecule enters a nucleus; receptors labelled RAR and RXR pair and dock on a short DNA element.
scenes.narration: In the nucleus, it binds the retinoic acid receptor, RAR. RAR pairs with its partner, RXR, on short DNA sequences called response elements.

scenes.tts: Hox A one and Hox B one carry these elements. In cell culture, three prime Hox genes respond to lower doses than five prime genes.
scenes.caption: Hoxa1 and Hoxb1 carry these elements. In cell culture, 3′ Hox genes respond to lower doses than 5′ genes.
scenes.visual: The receptor pair docks on a generic response element beside Hoxb1, with Hoxa1 alongside; no upstream or downstream position is drawn. Threshold lines on the curve, labelled cell culture, illustration: lower for 3′ genes, higher for 5′ genes.
scenes.narration: Hoxa1 and Hoxb1 carry these elements. In cell culture, 3′ Hox genes respond to lower doses than 5′ genes.

scenes.tts: In a simple threshold model, then, fewer Hox genes come on toward the front, where the signal is lower.
scenes.visual: Label: simple threshold model, an illustration. Where the curve falls below each threshold line, that gene's domain ends.
scenes.narration: In a simple threshold model, then, fewer Hox genes come on toward the front, where the signal is lower.

scenes.tts: Predict. Give mouse embryos extra retinoic acid at an early stage. Which way should the Hox edges move?
scenes.visual: Question card: pour in extra. Arrows point both ways along the row.
scenes.narration: Predict. Give mouse embryos extra retinoic acid at an early stage. Which way should the Hox edges move?

scenes.tts: Forward. In nineteen ninety-two, Marshall, Krumlauf, Lumsden and colleagues found the hindbrain Hox domains changed.
scenes.caption: Forward. In 1992, Marshall, Krumlauf, Lumsden and colleagues found the hindbrain Hox domains changed.
scenes.visual: Selected Hox domains expand forward into r2 and r3; the other edges are left faded. Credit card: Marshall, Krumlauf, Lumsden and colleagues, 1992.
scenes.narration: Forward. In 1992, Marshall, Krumlauf, Lumsden and colleagues found the hindbrain Hox domains changed.

scenes.tts: Rhombomeres two and three shifted toward the identity of four and five. Too much signal shows a response, not the normal role.
scenes.visual: r2 and r3 take on the colours of r4 and r5. Caption: too much shows a response, not the normal role.
scenes.narration: Rhombomeres two and three shifted toward the identity of four and five. Too much signal shows a response, not the normal role.

scenes.tts: Predict. Now block the drain. Mice lacking Cyp twenty-six A one clear less retinoic acid at the front. What changes?
scenes.caption: Predict. Now block the drain. Mice lacking Cyp26a1 clear less retinoic acid at the front. What changes?
scenes.visual: Question card: block the drain. The drain at the front is plugged.
scenes.narration: Predict. Now block the drain. Mice lacking Cyp26a1 clear less retinoic acid at the front. What changes?

scenes.tts: The front shifts: the front of the hindbrain looked partly transformed toward a more posterior character.
scenes.visual: The plugged drain at the front clears less retinoic acid; front segments tint partly toward posterior colours. No concentration curve is drawn. Credit: Abu-Abed and colleagues, 2001.
scenes.narration: The front shifts: the front of the hindbrain looked partly transformed toward a more posterior character.

scenes.tts: Remove the tap instead, in mice lacking Raldh two, and the posterior hindbrain is poorly patterned.
scenes.caption: Remove the tap instead, in mice lacking Raldh2, and the posterior hindbrain is poorly patterned.
scenes.visual: The tap is removed; the back of the row loses its colours.
scenes.narration: Remove the tap instead, in mice lacking Raldh2, and the posterior hindbrain is poorly patterned.

scenes.tts: Changing the signal sets the direction, not the exact edges.
scenes.caption: Changing the signal sets the direction, not the exact edges.
scenes.visual: Caption: direction, not exact edges. A Hox cluster sketch, 3′ end at the head side.
scenes.narration: Changing the signal sets the direction, not the exact edges.

scenes.tts: In the hindbrain, group two genes reach farther forward than group one. Yet three prime genes need less signal. So other inputs help set those edges.
scenes.caption: In the hindbrain, group 2 genes reach farther forward than group 1. Yet 3′ genes need less signal. So other inputs help set those edges.
scenes.visual: The grid: Hoxa2 and Hoxb2 edges sit in front of Hoxb1. Label: in the hindbrain the order bends.
scenes.narration: In the hindbrain, group 2 genes reach farther forward than group 1. Yet 3′ genes need less signal. So other inputs help set those edges.

scenes.tts: Retinoids are teratogens, agents that cause birth defects. In mouse and chick, extra retinoic acid early shifts the Hox code.
scenes.visual: Caption: teratogen, an agent that causes birth defects. The shifted grid from earlier.
scenes.narration: Retinoids are teratogens, agents that cause birth defects. In mouse and chick, extra retinoic acid early shifts the Hox code.

scenes.tts: It also disturbs the neural crest cells that build much of the face. In humans, this mechanism is inferred from animal work.
scenes.visual: Neural crest cells stream from the hindbrain toward a face outline. Caption: in humans, inferred from animal work.
scenes.narration: It also disturbs the neural crest cells that build much of the face. In humans, this mechanism is inferred from animal work.

scenes.tts: More early retinoic acid gives a more posterior code; the code helps set the neurons. Other inputs help draw the final edges.
scenes.visual: Closing card: more early retinoic acid, a more posterior code; the code helps set the neurons. Final edges: segment genes, local signals and repression.
scenes.narration: More early retinoic acid gives a more posterior code; the code helps set the neurons. Other inputs help draw the final edges.
